findings: The original scheduling/dependency/cancellation/group reservation methods are byte-identical.
After the first observed scheduling/race rejection, catch takes a snapshot of all remaining started tasks and awaits allSettled before fixture cleanup; no new scheduling pass occurs.
Successful race winner is removed before recording; drain records only remaining entries once. Late fulfilled fixtures reach the same retention callback before cleanup.

All settled failures are collected; distinct identities preserved. The original rejection appearing again in the running map is deduplicated. A single execution or cleanup-only failure is thrown unchanged, including undefined as an allowed rejection value.
Cleanup exception joins existing failures instead of masking them. Individual recordExecution failures during drain are captured and do not prevent other settled entries from being processed.
No new stop/abort/deadline authority, unbounded retry or new lifecycle layer. Existing node owners must settle their own promises.
